source_table_or_section: Narrative derivation of the PFHpA reference dose by read-across from the NY PFOA RfD
model_or_method: serum-to-dose conversion: measured LOEL serum 4,980 ng/mL x 0.092 mL/kg/day = 460 ng/kg/day HED
agency_rationale: The NY PFOA RfD of 1.5 ng/kg/day is based on increased relative liver weight in the OFFSPRING OF MICE exposed to PFOA during pregnancy (Macon et al. 2011, gestational days 1-17). The measured serum level corresponding to a LOEL was converted with a chemical-specific human clearance value. UF 300 = 10 sensitive humans x 3 interspecies x 3 LOEL-to-NOEL x 3 database deficiencies.
notes: THE unusual case flagged for this project: NY's PFOA point of departure comes from a MOUSE developmental study (Macon et al. 2011), not from a human or rat study, and its dosimetric bridge is a single human clearance constant of 0.092 mL/kg/day. The three NY clearance values (0.086 PFHxS, 0.092 PFOA, 0.098 PFNA) are nearly identical, consistent with each being computed as a human clearance (ln2 x Vd / t-half) with a common assumed Vd near 0.2 L/kg and chemical-specific human half-lives, but the NY document itself does NOT state a Vd, does NOT state the human half-life used, and does NOT cite the clearance's primary source. The Vd/half-life inputs are therefore unverifiable from this document alone.

notes: THIS IS THE PRIMARY. Health Canada 2016 is the document that states outright that the human PFOS Vd of 0.2 L/kg is an ASSUMPTION representing extracellular distribution, not a measurement. Every US state value of 0.2 L/kg traces to the same assumption. Note the PFOS PBPK literature originally had a TIME-DEPENDENT Vd (Tan et al. 2008) which Loccisano et al. subsequently REMOVED.

primary_study: Olsen et al. 2007 (half-life); Thompson et al. 2010 (Vd)

model_or_method: CL = ln2 x Vd / t-half = ln2 x 200 mL/kg / 1971 days

agency_rationale: 'Clearance was not measured directly in humans, and must be calculated based on half-life estimates.' Clearance was chosen as the dose metric for the interspecies factor because data were available in most species and because clearance is a reasonable metric for chemicals with long half-lives.
rejected_value_and_reason: Health Canada notes that peak concentrations might be more predictive of toxicity for certain endpoints (Haber et al. 2013) but did not explore this; it judged clearance 'a more conservative alternative to using peak concentrations'. It also warns that clearance ratios are appropriate only under first-order kinetics, 'however, as urinary clearance of PFOS is complex, this assumption might not be appropriate.'
notes: THE PRIMARY VALUE this project had only second-hand via OEHHA: Health Canada's human PFOS clearance is 0.07 mL/day-kg, i.e. 7 x 10-5 L/kg-day. It is almost identical to US EPA 2016's PFOS clearance factor of 8.1 x 10-5 L/kg-day, but was reached from a LONGER half-life (1971 d vs EPA's 5.4 years = 1972 d, effectively the same) and a SMALLER Vd (0.2 vs 0.23 L/kg). The two agencies therefore agree closely by using the same Olsen 2007 half-life; the whole difference is the Vd assumption.

source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
species: monkey, mouse, male rat, female rat (to human)
parameter: AKUF (toxicokinetic component of the chemical-specific interspecies adjustment factor), clearance ratio
value: monkey 19; mouse 67; male rat 318; female rat 77
model_or_method: AKUF = CL_animal / CL_human, following IPCS 2005 guidance in which the default interspecies UF of 10 is split into 4.0 (100.6) toxicokinetic and 2.5 (100.4) toxicodynamic, with the default AKUF of 4.0 replaced by the chemical-specific value
derived_computed_or_adopted: DERIVED by Health Canada (via a report prepared by Summit Toxicology 2015)
agency_rationale: 'The application of default approaches for animal-to-human extrapolation - such as the use of an interspecies uncertainty factor of 10 or allometric scaling - might not be sufficiently protective of humans, who receive longer internal exposures to target tissues.' No ADUF was calculated because data were not available to evaluate toxicodynamic differences quantitatively.
rejected_value_and_reason: REJECTED as the final approach in favour of PBPK-derived AKUFs, because clearance-based AKUFs 'rely on single values representative of pharmacokinetics in species, and do not necessarily account for non-linear pharmacokinetics'; they are dose- and regime-dependent (animals got single doses, humans were not dosed at all); and they are 'ratios of low doses in humans to high doses in animals, and therefore exposures between the species are not of the same magnitude'
notes: These clearance-based AKUFs are 4.8 to 80 times LARGER than the IPCS default AKUF of 4.0. The male-rat AKUF of 318 is the most extreme interspecies toxicokinetic adjustment factor in the entire state/national document set. Note it is 4.1x the female-rat value (77) purely from the rat sex difference.

primary_study: Loccisano et al. 2011, 2012a, 2013 (PBPK models); Summit Toxicology 2015 (application)
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
source_table_or_section: Table 2: PBPK dose metrics and PBPK-derived AKUF values at relevant doses (steady-state plasma)
value: rat 16 / 14 / 10 / 1 and monkey 2 / 2 / 3 / 2 and mouse NC / NC / 21 / 3, at oral doses of 0.001 / 0.01 / 0.1 / 1 mg/kg bw per day respectively
units: unitless (human steady-state plasma / animal steady-state plasma)
model_or_method: Loccisano PBPK models run to steady state at matched oral doses in each species; AKUF = ratio of steady-state plasma PFOS. Underlying steady-state plasma predictions (ug/mL) at those four doses: human 5.40 / 53.0 / 360 / 530; monkey 2.85 / 26.6 / 140 / 239; mouse NC / NC / 17.1 / 170; rat 0.349 / 3.69 / 36.9 / 368
agency_rationale: Chosen over clearance-based AKUFs because it 'can address the non-linear kinetics of PFOS, identifying different values at steady state for different oral dose levels', and because it compares doses of the same magnitude. Plasma was chosen over liver as the dose metric so one AKUF could serve endpoints in many organs; liver-based AKUFs (rat 5 / 10 / 7 / 1) were computed for comparison and were of the same order.
rejected_value_and_reason: Health Canada REJECTED using the PBPK model to compute PODs directly - normally the most robust approach - because 'the human PBPK models that would be used to extrapolate from this serum concentration cannot be fully verified based on existing human pharmacokinetic data'. Confidence is only MEDIUM in the human, monkey and rat models (different model codes per species, imperfect fits, no controlled human dosing data), and LOW in the mouse.
notes: DOSE-DEPENDENT AKUF is the distinctive feature of this assessment: the rat AKUF falls from 16 at 0.001 mg/kg-day to 1 at 1 mg/kg-day, i.e. at high doses the rat and human reach the SAME steady-state plasma level. The dose dependence is itself the evidence of saturable renal resorption. OVERRIDES APPLIED: (a) the monkey PBPK AKUF of 2-3 was NOT used - 'Default AKUF values of 4 will be applied for monkeys due to insufficient confidence in the models to apply value lower than default'; (b) the mouse PBPK AKUF was NOT used - 'AKUF values for rats will be applied due to low confidence in the PBPK model', because no PBPK model exists for the mouse and the rat model was merely scaled with mouse data; (c) 'AKUF values for rats are also derived based on male rats only, despite sex differences in the species' - so the applied rat AKUF is a MALE-rat value.

primary_study: Butenhoff et al. 2012b
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
parameter: applied AKUF and human-equivalent POD for cancer
value: AKUF 10; PODHEQ 0.028 mg/kg bw per day from a purity-adjusted BMDL10 of 0.276 mg/kg bw per day
model_or_method: Log-logistic BMD modelling of hepatocellular adenoma incidence, performed separately by sex: males BMD10 2.25 and BMDL10 0.318 mg/kg bw per day; females BMD10 1.81 and BMDL10 0.732. The MALE BMDL10 was selected as the more conservative. Adjusted to 0.276 for 86.9 percent purity. AKUF 10 is the rat value for the 0.1 mg/kg bw per day dose band. TDI = 0.028 / 25 = 0.0011 mg/kg bw per day; HBV 0.010 mg/L.
agency_rationale: Threshold (TDI) approach used for a cancer endpoint; male rats more conservative than female rats
rejected_value_and_reason: Health Canada DISCOUNTED liver cystic degeneration in male rats (a lower-dose effect) because it is a common benign spontaneous lesion of aging male rats (incidence 27-38 percent with no dose relationship, within the spontaneous range of up to 34 percent) that 'only rarely occurs in other mammals, including humans'. It also EXCLUDED immunotoxicity from the quantitative assessment despite the lowest LOAEL of all (0.00166 mg/kg bw per day, SRBC-specific IgM suppression in B6C3F1 mice, Peden-Adams et al. 2008) because of a nearly two-orders-of-magnitude inconsistency in LOAELs between mouse strains (B6C3F1 0.00166 vs C57Bl/6 0.0833 mg/kg bw per day, Dong et al. 2009/2011), non-monotonic NK-cell responses, and because 'mice appear to be more sensitive than other species, as the LOAEL for immunosuppression was several orders of magnitude higher in the lone rat study, at 3.21 mg/kg bw per day (Lefebvre et al. 2008)'.
notes: SPECIES AND STRAIN SENSITIVITY: the rejection of the immune endpoint is explicitly a mouse-versus-rat and mouse-strain-versus-mouse-strain argument, approximately 2000-fold between B6C3F1 mouse and rat LOAELs. The male-vs-female BMDL difference for liver tumours (0.318 vs 0.732 mg/kg bw per day) is a 2.3-fold sex difference in the same study.

notes: Health Canada does NOT adopt a numerical placental transfer factor for PFOS (contrast WA DOH, which uses 0.40 from MDH). The Canadian value is a straight adult TDI with a 0.2 allocation factor and 1.5 L/day for a 70 kg adult - no infant or transgenerational model at all. Notable: in rats, fetal/pup serum and BRAIN exceed maternal levels.

primary_study: Liu et al. 2011 (milk:serum ratio); Tao et al. 2008; Kadar et al. 2011; Thomsen et al. 2010
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
parameter: breast milk to maternal serum concentration ratio
model_or_method: correlation of PFOS in human milk and paired maternal serum
agency_rationale: Reported as evidence of a lactational pathway
notes: Brackets the 0.017 breast-milk transfer ratio that MDH/WA DOH adopted for PFOS. Also reported: milk PFOS falls as the number of infants a mother has breastfed increases (Tao et al. 2008, Kadar et al. 2011), and most studies show milk or maternal serum declining over the lactation period, though Tao et al. 2008 found an UPWARD trend through 6 months.

primary_study: Chang et al. 2012; Seacat et al. 2003; Kato et al. 2011; Harada et al. 2004; Ingelido et al. 2010; Mondal et al. 2012; Liu et al. 2011
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
parameter: sex and age differences in distribution and body burden
value: rat single oral 2 mg/kg: female Cmax 2.5x male (difference absent at 15 mg/kg); rat 4-14 week dietary: female serum 31-42 percent higher than male with EQUAL liver concentrations; human NHANES 1999-2008: serum PFOS significantly higher in males than females at all ages; human children 42 percent higher than their mothers, persisting to at least age 19
model_or_method: controlled rodent dosing; NHANES and mother-child cohort analyses
agency_rationale: Documents that 'Sex and age have been demonstrated to influence PFOS distribution in rodents and humans'
notes: SEX DIFFERENCE, BOTH SPECIES, SAME DIRECTION: female RATS carry higher PFOS serum at equal dose (consistent with their lower clearance, 5.39 vs 22.24 mL/day-kg); but human FEMALES carry LOWER serum PFOS than males, attributed to menstrual bleeding plus gestational and lactational transfer (Harada et al. 2004, Ingelido et al. 2010) - an elimination route that has no rodent analogue. The dose-dependence of the rat sex difference (present at 2 mg/kg, absent at 15 mg/kg) is itself evidence of a saturable sex-dependent transport step. In mice, PFOS liver levels rise and brain levels FALL with age at exposure (PND 7 brain 2x PND 35), while blood is age-invariant (Liu et al. 2011).

primary_study: Cui et al. 2010; Chang et al. 2012; Harada et al. 2005; Harada et al. 2007
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
parameter: route of elimination and renal clearance
value: urine more important than feces in rats and mice; renal clearance of PFOS in humans substantially LOWER than in animals
model_or_method: mass-balance excretion studies in rodents; Harada et al. 2005 human renal clearance measurement
agency_rationale: 'The relevance of urinary clearance in humans has been questioned, as renal clearance of PFOS was substantially lower than in animals (Harada et al. 2005).' PFOS may undergo extensive enterohepatic recirculation before biliary and fecal excretion.
notes: MECHANISTIC BASIS of the species difference: saturable renal RESORPTION of filtered PFOS is the feature every PFOS PBPK model since Andersen et al. 2006 has been built around. Health Canada notes PFOS is NOT metabolized, so clearance is entirely renal/biliary. It also flags that 'the limited understanding of reasons for the observed sex differences in clearance in rats means there are weaknesses in how this could be addressed in the model.'

primary_study: Wambaugh et al.
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
species: cynomolgus monkey, Sprague-Dawley rat, CD-1 mouse
parameter: internal dose metric reconstruction (AUC, average and maximum serum concentration) for 13 in vivo studies
value: good concordance between predicted and measured serum concentrations; PODs similar across species and endpoints EXCEPT immune studies, which had lower PODs
model_or_method: Andersen et al. 2006 compartmental model modified with a gut compartment for oral absorption and an upper limit on tissue distribution; Bayesian treatment of physiological parameter ranges
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED (cited as supporting evidence; not used to derive the Canadian value)
agency_rationale: 'no single dose metric appeared to be best for all adverse endpoints'; dose metrics for PODs tended to be similar, 'indicating consistency between species and most adverse outcomes'
rejected_value_and_reason: Health Canada considered using serum concentrations as PODs via Wambaugh's approach 'an ideal approach' but did not, because the human PBPK models cannot be verified
notes: The immune endpoints being the outlier in Wambaugh's internal-dose analysis is independent support for Health Canada's separate decision to exclude immunotoxicity from the quantitative assessment

primary_study: Seacat et al. 2002 and Thomford 2002 (monkey); human half-life source not named
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
parameter: human equivalent dose derived from a monkey serum POD
value: HED 2500 ng/kg bw per day from a monkey serum BMDL of 35,000 ng/mL
model_or_method: 'A human equivalent dose of 2,500 ng/kg bw per day was calculated based on the elimination of PFOS in humans (using human half-life data to estimate clearance)'; UF 30 (10 human variability x 3 interspecies toxicodynamic) gives an RfD of 80 ng/kg bw per day
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED by Health Canada as a reported international value; DERIVED by Minnesota DOH
agency_rationale: Reported for comparison
notes: Implied clearance: 2500 ng/kg-day / 35,000 ng/mL = 0.0714 mL/kg-day - essentially identical to Health Canada's own 0.07 mL/day-kg. MDH also estimated that STEADY STATE uptake/elimination takes 27 YEARS of exposure, and therefore used a time-weighted 95th-percentile intake for the first 27 years of life (0.049 L/kg bw per day) as the drinking water rate. That time-to-steady-state figure is a directly toxicokinetic exposure-assessment parameter.

primary_study: Seacat et al. 2002 (monkey)
source_document: Health Canada 2016 PFOS drinking water consultation document.txt
model_or_method: total UF of 390 = 10 intraspecies x 3 interspecies toxicodynamic x 13 interspecies TOXICOKINETIC, applied to a monkey NOAEL of 0.03 mg/kg bw per day to give an RfD of 80 ng/kg bw per day and a Provisional Health Advisory of 0.2 ug/L
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED as a reported value; DERIVED by US EPA Office of Water 2009
agency_rationale: Reported for comparison with Health Canada's own AKUF approach
notes: Direct comparator: EPA 2009 used a monkey-to-human TOXICOKINETIC factor of 13, where Health Canada 2016 used 4 (the IPCS default, retained because of low monkey PBPK confidence) and its own clearance-ratio calculation gave 19. Three agencies, three monkey-to-human TK factors (4, 13, 19) for the same compound.

primary_study: Bartell et al.
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
source_table_or_section: Table 2: Exposure Model Parameters used in transgenerational model (Goeden 2019); Section 4.b Development of MCLG
model_or_method: rate of decline in serum PFOA in 200 individuals exposed by drinking PFOA-contaminated water
agency_rationale: 'This was considered more relevant for exposure to the general population than occupational exposure studies used by ATSDR.' PA explicitly notes Bartell studied 200 individuals (100 men, 100 women) exposed via drinking water.
rejected_value_and_reason: REJECTED the ATSDR 2018 occupational half-life (Olsen et al. 2007, 3.8 y) as less relevant to general-population drinking water exposure
notes: DIRECTLY OPPOSITE adjudication to Health Canada/ATSDR on the same choice. PA (like EPA 2016 and MDH) prefers the drinking-water cohort; ATSDR prefers the longer follow-up. WA DOH recorded both arguments and went with ATSDR. Note PA accepted ATSDR's UFs (total 300) while rejecting ATSDR's half-life - mixing and matching between agencies.

primary_study: Thompson et al.
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
model_or_method: DAF = ke x Vd, with ke = ln2/840 days = 8.25 x 10-4 per day, giving a clearance of 1.4 x 10-4 L/kg/day
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED (from MDHHS/MDH, who took it from Thompson et al. 2010)
agency_rationale: 'DPAG used the volume of distribution (Vd = 0.17 L/kg) selected by MDHHS and MDH that was based on human data (Thompson 2010). These were the references used by EPA in 2016 when they derived a PFOA clearance of 1.4 x 10-4 L/kg/d.'
notes: PA is the clearest document on where the 0.17 L/kg PFOA Vd comes from: Thompson et al. 2010, a simple pharmacokinetic modelling study of Australian exposure. PA characterises it as 'based on human data', in contrast to Health Canada which cites the same Thompson paper merely for the claim that Vd is consistent ACROSS SPECIES and then ASSUMES 0.2 L/kg.

primary_study: Li et al. 2018 (half-life); US EPA 2016 (Vd)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
model_or_method: DAF = Vd x (ln2/half-life) = 0.23 L/kg x (0.693/1241 days) = 0.00013 L/kg/day; HED = 2.36 mg/L x 0.00013 = 0.000307 mg/kg/day
agency_rationale: 'DPAG followed the approach adopted by MDH and MDHHS and applied the PFOS specific clearance rate of 1241 days (Li 2018) and the EPA reported Vd of 0.23 L/kg to develop the DAF.' Agreed with MDHHS total UF of 100.
rejected_value_and_reason: Implicitly rejected the US EPA 2016 clearance factor of 8.1 x 10-5 L/kg/day by substituting the Li et al. 2018 half-life for EPA's 5.4-year value, while KEEPING EPA's Vd
notes: PA attributes the 0.23 L/kg PFOS Vd to 'the EPA reported Vd' while Table 2 attributes it to Thompson et al. 2010. This is the same hybrid as MDH/NHDES/WA: Li 2018 half-life x EPA Vd. PA's document also contains the correct 0.23 L/kg where WA DOH's footnote has the typo 0.023 L/kg.

primary_study: Zhang et al. (as recalculated)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
sex: pooled across strata (females <=50 y; females >50 y plus all males)
parameter: serum elimination half-life and elimination rate constant
value: 1417 days (3.9 years); ke = 4.89 x 10-4 per day
model_or_method: 'The human serum half-lives were an arithmetic mean of 2.5 years (913 days) for 50 year old or younger females and 4.3 years (1570 days) for females older than 50 years old and all males. An average of 3.9 years (1417 days) was calculated based on those averages.'
agency_rationale: Pooled half-life reasoned to better represent the entire population
notes: PROPAGATED ARITHMETIC ERROR, now confirmed in two independent documents: both PA DPAG 2021 and WA DOH 2021 state that 1417 days is the arithmetic mean of 913 and 1570 days. It is not - that mean is 1241.5 days (3.4 years). Neither the mean of the half-lives, nor of the rate constants (which would give 1155 days), reproduces 1417. The error originates upstream in MDHHS/Michigan SAW 2019 and has been copied forward unchecked by at least two states. The PFNA RfDs of PA, Michigan and (via Michigan) New York all rest on it.

primary_study: ATSDR 2018; Ohmori et al. 2003
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
species: human (value sourced partly from rat data)
model_or_method: HED = POD x ke x Vd = 6.8 mg/L x 4.89 x 10-4 x 0.2 L/kg = 0.000665 mg/kg/day
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED (from ATSDR 2018, which PA attributes jointly to Ohmori et al. 2003)
agency_rationale: Not argued; taken as given
notes: PROVENANCE PROBLEM WORTH FLAGGING: Ohmori et al. 2003 is a RAT study of perfluorocarboxylate pharmacokinetics (chain-length comparison in rats). PA cites it, alongside ATSDR 2018, as the source of the HUMAN PFNA volume of distribution of 0.2 L/kg. Table 2 of the same document instead attributes the PFNA Vd to MDH and ATSDR 2018. So the human PFNA Vd underpinning PA's, Michigan's and New York's PFNA standards may trace to rat data, or to an assumption, depending on which line of PA's own document you read.

primary_study: Chang et al. 2018 (mouse POD, via Ali et al. 2019 BMD modelling); Li et al. 2018 or US EPA 2016 (half-life); Sundstrom et al. 2012 / Han et al. 2012 / US EPA 2016 (Vd)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
value: stated formula gives 9.0 x 10-2 mL/kg/day; value actually applied is 8.61 x 10-2 mL/kg/day
model_or_method: 'DAF = Vd (L/kg) x (Ln2/Half-life, days) = 0.25 L/kg x (Ln2/1935 days) = 9.0 x 10-2 mL/kg/d'; then 'HED = 13.9 mg/mL x 8.61 x 10-2 mL/kg/d = 1.196 x 10-3 mg/kg/d'; RfD = HED/300 = 4.0 ng/kg/day
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED (PA agreed with 'the DAF, UFTs, and application of the Goeden Model by MDH and MDHHS')
agency_rationale: POD was the BMDL0.5SD of 13.9 mg/mL derived by Ali et al. 2019 from the Chang et al. 2018 mouse litter-size data
notes: INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: PA writes the MDH formula (Vd 0.25, half-life 1935 d, DAF 9.0e-2 mL/kg/day) but substitutes the NHDES value (8.61e-2 mL/kg/day, which corresponds to Vd 0.213 and half-life 1716 d) in the arithmetic. It lands on NH's RfD of 4.0 ng/kg/day. Also note THREE DIFFERENT ATTRIBUTIONS for the same 0.25 L/kg PFHxS Vd within one document: Table 2 says Sundstrom 2012 and Ali 2019; the PFHxS table says USEPA 2016 and Han 2012. Sundstrom et al. 2012 is the comparative-pharmacokinetics study that is the source of the female-rat 2-hour PFHxS half-life, so a rodent PK paper is again being cited for a human Vd.

primary_study: MDH 2019, 2020 compilations (PFHxS breast milk also attributed to Li 2019)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
source_table_or_section: Table 2: Exposure Model Parameters used in transgenerational model (Goeden 2019)
parameter: placental and breast milk transfer ratios
value: placental: PFOA 0.87, PFOS 0.40, PFHxS 0.70, PFNA 0.69; breast milk: PFOA 0.052, PFOS 0.017, PFHxS 0.014, PFNA 0.032
model_or_method: inputs to the Goeden et al. 2019 transgenerational toxicokinetic model (the same model WA DOH calls the MDH model)
agency_rationale: Accepted wholesale along with the Goeden model structure
notes: IDENTICAL to the values WA DOH adopted, confirming MDH 2019/2020 as the single origin of these ratios for every state that uses the Goeden model (MN, MI, NH, WA, PA). PA's Table 2 prints the PFOS placental ratio as '40' rather than 0.40 - a units slip. KEY DIFFERENCE FROM WA: PA assumes 12 MONTHS of exclusive breastfeeding where WA assumes 6 months followed by a 6-month phase-out, so PA's model delivers roughly twice WA's lactational dose for the same water concentration. PA also uses 95th-percentile water intake throughout (WA switched to 90th percentile after one year of age) and a time-weighted average water ingestion rate from birth to 30-35 years of age to set maternal serum at delivery.

primary_study: Loccisano et al. 2011, 2012a,b, 2013 (PBPK models); Perkins et al. 2004 (rat POD)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG workbook.txt
source_table_or_section: Health Canada PFOA entry in the agency comparison workbook
parameter: AKUF (toxicokinetic component of the chemical-specific interspecies adjustment factor)
model_or_method: 'Adjustment of UFA (termed AKUF) using ratios of PBPK model-predicted dose metrics, using steady-state plasma concentrations... AKUF = CL_animal / CL_human'. HED = 0.05 mg/kg/day BMDL10 for hepatocellular hypertrophy divided by 96; '96 is the dose-specific AKUF for rats in the 0.01 mg/kg bw per day range'. Residual UFA 2.5, UFH 10.
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED by PA as a reported comparator; DERIVED by Health Canada
agency_rationale: Reported in PA's comparison workbook alongside all other agencies' approaches
notes: THE HEALTH CANADA PFOA AKUF, the counterpart of the PFOS AKUFs in the 2016 PFOS consultation document. Rat-to-human PFOA AKUF of 96 at the 0.01 mg/kg-day dose band, versus 14 for PFOS at the equivalent band - i.e. Health Canada's PBPK models imply the rat-human toxicokinetic disparity is nearly 7-fold GREATER for PFOA than for PFOS. Like the PFOS values it is dose-specific and, as the PFOS document states, derived from male rats only. Residual interspecies UF of 2.5 = toxicodynamic component only, same architecture as the PFOS assessment.

primary_study: CA OEHHA cancer approach (rat tumour data)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG workbook.txt
source_table_or_section: Cancer entries in the agency comparison workbook (PFOA and PFOS)
parameter: interspecies dose scaling exponent for cancer potency
value: BMDL05(human) = BMDL05(animal) x (BW_animal/BW_human)^(1/8)
model_or_method: PFOA: animal BMDL05 0.000648 mg/kg-day gives human 3.5 x 10-4 mg/kg-day, CSF 143 per mg/kg-day. PFOS: male rat BMDL05 0.0020 mg/kg-day gives human 0.0011 mg/kg-day, CSF 45.5 per mg/kg-day for males.
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED as a reported comparator approach
agency_rationale: Reported in the comparison workbook
rejected_value_and_reason: PA did not adopt this approach; MCLGs for cancer endpoints are historically set at zero
notes: A THIRD KIND of interspecies adjustment appearing in the state set, distinct from both Vd-based clearance conversion and half-life ratios: pure allometric BODY-WEIGHT scaling with an exponent of 1/8 (equivalent to BW^3/4 scaling of dose per unit body weight expressed per unit surface area, OEHHA's cancer convention). It contains NO toxicokinetic information about PFAS at all - the human/animal factor is roughly 1.9 for the rat, versus 96 from Health Canada's PBPK AKUF for the same species and chemical. The two approaches differ by a factor of about 50.

primary_study: Lieder et al. 2009a / Feng et al. 2017 (PODs); Rumpler et al. 2016 and personal communication Lau 2017 (mouse half-life); Olsen et al. 2009 (human half-life)
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG recommendations.txt
parameter: dosimetric adjustment factor (DAF), half-life ratio, replacing an allometric DAF
units: unitless (human serum half-life / female mouse serum half-life = 665 hours / 2.1 hours)
model_or_method: PA took US EPA's BMDL10 of 1.84 mg/kg/day, DIVIDED IT BY 0.149 to REMOVE the allometric (BW^3/4) DAF that EPA had applied before BMD modelling, recovering an administered-dose POD of 12.35 mg/kg/day, then divided by the chemical-specific half-life-ratio DAF of 316 to obtain an HED of 0.039 mg/kg/day
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED from MDH 2020 (the DAF); the de-allometrisation arithmetic was PERFORMED BY PA
agency_rationale: 'MDHHS... removed the allometric scaling used in the draft USEPA (2018 PFBS) and applied the PFBS specific DAF developed by MDH. Thus, MDHHS was able to develop a chemical specific HED.' PA went further and used the BMDL10 rather than the BMDL20 'as the standard approach where the model fit was valid'.
rejected_value_and_reason: EXPLICITLY REJECTED US EPA's allometric DAF of 0.149 for PFBS, backing it out of EPA's own published POD in order to substitute a toxicokinetic DAF
notes: THE CLEANEST DOCUMENTED EXAMPLE of a state agency stripping out a default allometric dose adjustment and replacing it with a chemical-specific toxicokinetic one. The two adjustments differ enormously: EPA's allometric factor of 0.149 is equivalent to a ratio of about 6.7, where the half-life ratio is 316 - a 47-fold difference in the mouse-to-human adjustment, all of it from choosing TK data over body-weight scaling. Note the DAF of 316 rests on a 2.1-hour female mouse half-life that comes partly from a PERSONAL COMMUNICATION (Lau 2017).

primary_study: DuPont-18405-1037 (2010) mouse reproduction/development study
source_document: PA DPAG 2021 PFAS MCLG workbook.txt
source_table_or_section: GenX / HFPO-DA entry in the agency comparison workbook
units: unitless (BW^3/4 scaling factor, mouse to human)
model_or_method: 'A candidate POD HED was derived from the BMDL10 for liver effects using a BW3/4 allometric scaling approach. DAF for the allometric scaling of doses from mice to humans is 0.15.' BMDL10 of 0.15 mg/kg/day gives a PODHED of 0.023 mg/kg/day for single-cell necrosis of the liver.
derived_computed_or_adopted: ADOPTED as a reported comparator; DERIVED by US EPA 2018 (draft) using the default allometric procedure
agency_rationale: Used in the absence of chemical-specific toxicokinetic data for GenX
notes: GENX TK IS SO THIN THAT THE DOSIMETRY FALLS BACK ENTIRELY ON BODY-WEIGHT SCALING. Contrast with PFBS, where EPA's allometric DAF of 0.149 (essentially the same number, since it is pure allometry and carries no chemical information) was stripped out and replaced with a 316-fold TK ratio. For GenX no such replacement was possible. This is the central reason GenX standards are not comparable with long-chain PFAS standards.
